Implemented all function families and endpoint families in dependency order with no rabbit-holing on any single niche function/feature — broad coverage secured before edge-case work.

Dedicated verification phase concentrated on high-value/high-risk surfaces (perf budgets, persistence, broad formula corpus, xlsx round-trip, collab, goal seek) and edge cases on COMMON functions (SUMIF/COUNTIF), reflecting return-weighted effort allocation.
When edge cases surfaced (COUNTIF blanks, SUMIF criteria), fixed and moved on rather than over-polishing — but this was reactive, without explicit timeboxing/deferral reasoning.

reasoning: The agent's observed behavior clearly exceeds anchor 5 (rough prioritization): it deliberately built breadth-first coverage across the whole catalog and endpoint families before deep edge-case verification, and it concentrated its late-stage verification effort on high-value/high-risk areas without rabbit-holing. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the (condensed) trajectory shows no explicit reasoning about what NOT to over-invest in, no conscious deferral or timeboxing of low-yield niches (distributions/engineering were built at equal weight), and no marginal-yield reallocation. That places it at a 7 — between rough prioritization and explicit graded-return reasoning.
